name: Demo identity and ownership
risk: Unauthorized creation, reading or status change
contract: Known X-Demo-Actor identifies a synthetic actor; it is a simulation, not authentication. Only customers may submit and only for their fixture member. Customers may read their own claims; adjuster, finance and auditor may read all. Only adjusters approve; only finance actors pay. Unknown actors and forbidden operations return HTTP 403 without state changes.

name: Submission and duplicate identity
risk: Duplicate claims or invalid stored records
contract: Require claim_id, member_id, service, amount_cents; optionally in_network, authorized, formulary. IDs are case-sensitive ASCII letters/digits/hyphen/underscore, 3–48 characters, beginning with a letter or digit. Policy and active status come from member fixtures. Validate HC rules before saving. A coverage denial is HTTP 422 and stores nothing. A successful evaluation creates submitted revision 1, HTTP 201. An existing claim ID conflicts globally with HTTP 409 DUPLICATE_CLAIM. A rejected ID can be corrected and reused.

name: Ordered claim lifecycle
risk: Skipping approval, repeating an action, or invalid transitions
contract: Allowed transitions are submitted to approved by an adjuster, then approved to paid by finance. All other state transitions return HTTP 409 INVALID_TRANSITION. Only approved and paid are valid target names; malformed targets return HTTP 400. Wrong-role actions return 403 before checking the current status. Successful actions increment revision once; failed actions preserve status and revision.

name: Simulated payment exactly once
contract: Entering paid creates one simulated ledger row whose amount equals the stored evaluation payout, including zero payout. A unique claim_id in the ledger prevents a second entry. No real money moves. Replaying paid returns 409 and leaves the original ledger entry unchanged. Status, ledger and event changes commit atomically.

name: Event and provenance evidence
risk: Unexplained state changes or losing the evaluated contract
contract: Each successful submission or transition appends one ordered event with actor, timestamp, from/to status, rule and revision. Failed actions append no success event. The stored evaluation and normalized request remain unchanged after approval/payment. Evidence exports include the claim, ordered events, ledger row and workflow contract hash. Local history is not tamper-proof.

name: Persistence and isolation
risk: Partial writes, concurrent duplicates, or test contamination
contract: SQLite transactions cover each state mutation. Concurrent same-ID submissions yield one creation and one conflict; concurrent payment attempts yield one transition and one conflict. A storage error rolls back status, event and ledger changes. Committed claims survive reopening the database. Automated tests use temporary databases distinct from the interactive database.
